newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian prosecutor aims at PM for arms shipment.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian prosecutor aims at PM for arms shipment.

text.p: Cambodia's military court on Tuesday asked the national assembly to revoke First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's parliamentary immunity to clear the way for legal proceedings against him for alleged weapons smuggling.
A weapons shipment, seized at Cambodia's main port in late May, sparked a serious row between the country's two prime ministers and led to a tense standoff between their security forces.

"The military court prosecutor sent a letter to the president of the national assembly this afternoon requesting the suspension of his (Ranariddh's) parliamentary immunity in order to prosecute for the illegal import of weapons," an interior ministry official, who declined to be identified, told Reuters.
Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, Ranariddh's uneasy coalition partner, earlier called for legal action over the weapons shipment which he said Ranariddh was importing illegally.

The prince denied he was trying to smuggle the shipment of arms into the country and pointed out that his name was on the shipping documents. He said he was entitled to import the equipment for the use of his personal security force.
An official in Ranariddh's office dismissed Tuesday's request by the military court.
"It is really a ridiculous request. It's nonsense," said the official who declined to be identified.
"If he wanted to do it illegally why would he send his name on the shipping form," said the official.
Ranariddh told reporters at the time he needed weapons, including anti-tank weapons, to defend himself because Hun Sen had formidable military might, including tanks, at his call.

The two prime ministers' security forces confronted each other at Phnom Penh's military airport the day after the shipment was seized in what political analysts said at the time was the closest they had come to an armed clash.
The prime ministers' well-armed bodyguard units fought a gun battle in central Phnom Penh on June 17 over an unrelated dispute. Two of Ranariddh's men were killed in the battle.

The two prime misters have been at odds for more than a year over power-sharing in their fractured coalition government and more recently over how to deal with the disintegrating Khmer Rouge guerrilla force.
There has been growing international concern over political stability and violence in the country in recent weeks.
